notes:
Inbound self-serve signup from a Zendesk add-on buyer. Small founding team (18 engineering + product/support combined). Main ask: speed to POC on Hosted API, then decide on Dedicated later if volumes justify. Key features they called out: tool calling (create Jira tickets / trigger webhooks), stable structured JSON output for agent-facing summary cards, streaming for live agent assist, and predictable per-ticket cost.

Call snippets / paraphrase: "We want plug-and-play — get something in our app within a week and iterate prompts." Re: models: leaning open / quantized to control spend but want Redwood's perf profiles.

Security: SOC2 not required immediately, but audit logs and SSO + retention controls are must-haves before they go to customers. Data residency: currently US-only customers but will ask about EU later.

Pricing sensitivity: pilot budget limited (~$2k/mo). Typical workload: 200-800 support tickets/month; average ticket needs 1–2 API calls (summarize + structured fields). Peak bursts during business hours ~5–10 reqs/sec; steady-state 1–2/sec. Latency target: <= 300ms median for summary generation; acceptable tail up to 700ms during bursts.

Integration notes: backend processes ticket text -> call Redwood Hosted generation with function/tool calling enabled to create Jira issues or escalate to human. Want example integration snippet, sample prompt templates, and a basic eval harness (compare human summaries).

AE context: inbound lead via docs search on tool-calling. They signed up for free credits and completed basic onboarding. Opted to keep exploring self-serve but asked AE to help estimate cost and set up quick tech call.

Quote from CTO on call: "If the API is straightforward and cheap to scale, we'll swap out our heuristics immediately."
